title: mRNA-encoding CD19-targeting T cell engager for refractory immune thrombocytopenia.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the project's paper_context tool: Europe PMC reports the article is not open access, has no PubMed Central ID, no supplementary files, no linked databases and no text-mined accessions other than antibody/cell-line RRIDs (Research Resource Identifiers, which are catalogue numbers for reagents, not data). I separately queried NCBI elink from PubMed ID 42759514 to all linked databases (only other PubMed articles came back, no GEO, SRA, BioProject or dbGaP) and searched Zenodo for ABO2203 (the only hit is an unrelated AI-generated market-commentary note, not data). No data file of any kind was found to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study design and results comes from the abstract alone: lipid-nanoparticle mRNA encoding a CD19-targeting T cell engager (a molecule that pulls T cells onto B cells), tested in transgenic mice and in three patients with refractory secondary immune thrombocytopenia, with 6-month follow-up. The full text, methods and any data availability statement are behind the Cell paywall, and project rules forbid scraping the publisher site.

a1_downloadable.note: No data exists to download. Paywalled with no PubMed Central deposit, no supplementary files listed by Europe PMC, no repository accession anywhere (checked NCBI elink and Zenodo). Human trial immunophenotyping and clinical data of this kind is normally not deposited at all, or is controlled-access.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table exists, so nothing is a column. Any outcome (platelet count recovery, depth of B cell depletion) would have to be transcribed by hand out of figures in a paywalled PDF.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table of any kind is available: no flow cytometry values, no clinical covariates, no sequences.

a4_units_stated.note: Cannot be assessed, because no data file was obtainable. The abstract mentions platelet recovery and adverse-event grades but gives no numbers or units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Three patients. The checklist floor is roughly 1,500 labelled rows, or 400 for classification. Even counting repeated blood draws over 6 months, the independent unit is the patient and there are three. This alone is fatal.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small if it existed; size is the one thing that is not a problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: there is no download to compare against the paper's claims.

a8_label_provenance.note: The outcomes described (platelet counts, flow-cytometry B cell counts, adverse-event grades) are real physical measurements, not another model's output. This is the only Part A item that is genuinely fine.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with three treated patients and no released data, any model would be describing three individuals, not a population.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use pre-treatment blood and clinical measures to predict how deeply and durably B cells are removed after an mRNA-based therapy.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need each patient's baseline immune-cell counts, antibody levels, prior treatments and dose, with one row per patient or per follow-up visit. Verified count available: three patients, plus an unknown number of transgenic mice.
plain_idea.predict: Depth and duration of B cell depletion and platelet recovery, measured by flow cytometry of blood and bone marrow and by routine platelet counts in the hospital lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked, rheumatologists deciding who gets an in-vivo B cell depleting therapy would have a pre-treatment risk score; but with three patients the question cannot even be posed, let alone answered.

ml_idea: None viable. The only conceivable task — predicting depth or durability of B cell depletion from baseline patient features — needs hundreds of treated patients pooled across trials (for example the CASTLE basket trial and other CD19 CAR-T autoimmune cohorts), not this three-patient first-in-human report. Revisit only if a large multi-centre registry of in-vivo B cell depletion outcomes is ever released openly.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data exists to load, so every compute figure would be invented.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the sample size in the abstract: three patients. That took ten seconds and kills it outright; the absence of any deposited data confirms it.

verdict_reason: Three-patient first-in-human clinical report with no deposited data. Part A1 fails (paywalled, no PubMed Central deposit, no supplementary files, no accession in NCBI or Zenodo) and A5 fails by three orders of magnitude (n=3 patients versus a floor of ~400). A2, A3, A4 and A7 cannot even be assessed because there is no file to open. This is a therapeutics milestone paper, not a dataset.
